title: Linux Evolution and Popular Operating Systems

sections.title: Mission · What Kind of Linux System Am I Looking At?
paragraphs: Understand how Linux developed into an ecosystem of operating systems and recognize major Linux distributions, embedded Linux systems, and Linux's role in cloud computing. The exam is not asking you to become an expert administrator of every distribution.
sections.callout: WHAT KIND OF LINUX SYSTEM AM I LOOKING AT?

sections.title: Linux Is a Kernel
paragraphs: Linux technically refers to the Linux kernel, not one single operating system. The kernel is the core component that communicates between software and hardware and manages CPU, memory, devices, and processes.

Organizations and communities combine the Linux kernel with utilities, applications, package-management systems, desktop environments, and other software. The resulting complete operating system is called a Linux distribution, or distro.

sections.title: Linux Distributions
paragraphs: Different distributions exist because users and organizations have different requirements. A distribution may emphasize desktop usability, enterprise servers, stability, long-term support, development, embedded systems, or cloud computing.
sections.callout: Many distributions are built around the Linux kernel.

sections.title: Debian
paragraphs: Debian is a major community-developed Linux distribution known for stability, large software repositories, community development, and serving as the foundation for other distributions. Ubuntu is based on Debian.
sections.callout: Large community distribution that serves as the foundation for Ubuntu → Debian

sections.title: Ubuntu
paragraphs: Ubuntu is a popular Debian-based Linux distribution used across desktops, servers, development, and cloud environments. It aims to make Linux accessible while remaining useful professionally.

sections.title: Ubuntu LTS
paragraphs: LTS means Long Term Support. An Ubuntu LTS release receives extended maintenance and support compared with ordinary releases. Organizations often choose LTS when they value stability, predictability, and longer support periods.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company wants an Ubuntu server release intended to remain supported for a longer period.

sections.title: Red Hat
paragraphs: Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) is a commercial enterprise Linux distribution. Organizations may select enterprise distributions for vendor support, enterprise lifecycle management, stability, and commercial services.
sections.callout: Commercial enterprise Linux → Red Hat Enterprise Linux

sections.title: CentOS
paragraphs: CentOS has historically been closely associated with the Red Hat ecosystem. For Linux Essentials, recognize the relationship between CentOS and enterprise Linux environments rather than treating CentOS as an unrelated Linux family.

sections.title: SUSE and openSUSE
paragraphs: SUSE is a major name in enterprise Linux. openSUSE is associated with the broader SUSE ecosystem and community.
sections.callout: SUSE = ENTERPRISE · openSUSE = COMMUNITY-ORIENTED SUSE ECOSYSTEM

sections.title: Exam Trap — Distribution Relationships
paragraphs: Do not treat every Linux distribution as completely independent. The exam may test names and family relationships rather than obscure technical differences.

sections.title: Linux Mint
paragraphs: Linux Mint is a desktop-focused Linux distribution designed with ease of use in mind. It is closely associated with the Ubuntu and Debian ecosystem.

sections.title: Scientific Linux
paragraphs: Scientific Linux is a Linux distribution historically associated with scientific and research environments. Scientific is the distribution name, not a Linux command or special kernel.
sections.callout: Scientific or research Linux distribution → Scientific Linux

sections.title: Embedded Systems
paragraphs: Linux is not limited to desktop PCs and servers. An embedded system performs a particular function as part of a larger device. Linux can run in network appliances, smart devices, industrial systems, media devices, and single-board computers.
sections.callout: Linux knowledge reaches far beyond traditional PCs.

sections.title: Raspberry Pi
paragraphs: A Raspberry Pi is a small single-board computer commonly used for education, programming, electronics projects, home labs, automation, and embedded computing.
sections.callout: Small single-board computer used for Linux projects → Raspberry Pi

sections.title: Raspbian
paragraphs: Raspbian is historically associated with Debian-based Linux for the Raspberry Pi platform.
sections.callout: Raspberry Pi = HARDWARE · Raspbian = OPERATING SYSTEM

sections.title: Exam Trap — Raspberry Pi vs. Raspbian

table.caption: Do not reverse the hardware and software
rows: Linux operating system or distribution associated with Raspberry Pi

sections.title: Android
paragraphs: Android uses the Linux kernel. It demonstrates that Linux technology exists beyond traditional Linux desktops and servers.
sections.callout: Mobile operating system built using the Linux kernel → Android

sections.title: Linux in the Cloud
paragraphs: Linux is heavily used in cloud environments because it supports flexibility, automation, remote administration, broad server software, and efficient deployment. Linux command-line and server skills are therefore valuable in cloud computing.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: An administrator launches a virtual server at a cloud provider and installs Ubuntu Server. It is still a Linux system even though there is no physical server beside the administrator.
entries.recognitionCue: Virtual Linux servers hosted remotely → Linux in the cloud

Linux virtual machine at a cloud provider → Linux in the cloud
sections.callout: Recognize the family, platform, or deployment environment.
